title: Best vibe coded game?
author: Square_Reason_6490
selftext: What is the best vibe coded game you have seen? Meaning you pay 10$ to play? The Capybara Delivery game was  interesting but I wouldn’t wanna buy that and I’m board of it in 3mins. But impressed that was even possible

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: I think just the fact you are starting is great and has a lot finishing a game is super hard you should post it to itch to get more feedback that can help you see what works and what doesn’t I have had games for over 20 years from Indy to AAA and I’m still learning I would highly suggest you start small and finish than go big for your first joint you will also learn what sort of games you enjoy making art is a huge factor for a game being loved or not but you can reskin any game to feel very different from the look of the ui, the world, characters, VFX, sound etc. replacing any of those can greatly change the vibe of your game, it’s a lot tougher to get people to download and install your game than to try it on itch and itch will expose you to more players and tastes. I would never install a game from a random reddit thread, no offense to you, but the chances are too high of something very bad happening 🤣 Good luck!

comments.author: HoboSteeveJacko
comments.body:
I feel like my game Cellora is maybe a little more intentional than a vibe coded game but its a spatial strategy casual competitive digital game board. The game board is constructed by the players at the beginning of the match and then its like tic tac toe but you can get more tokens then 3 in a row and there can be up to 4 players.

https://preview.redd.it/1p4liv1je8dh1.jpeg?width=1898&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=ee0e99e202ae48ed230e01b017217bbdfcbbd4a9

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: **I asked for examples of vibe coded games. How is your game vibe coded?**

replies.author: HoboSteeveJacko
replies.body:
I mean the entire game was made using only claude ai. Its art, its code all done on ai. Most people would say this is a "vibe" coded game however it kinda depends on how you're defining vibe coded. I had to use my intuition as a player to decide how to tweak difficulty levels and how the game feel works and find bugs in the code. I have absolutely no background in systems engineering or coding. 

I guess decide for yourself if it's vibe coded. Im pretty open on answering any questions. Let me know if you need any further clarifying let me know. If I'm wrong sorry to bother but to me in most threads I'm taken at face value as a vibe coded slop game though none of those people took the time to play it either.

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Ahhh good point and I agree, I’m super open to the term vibe coded I shouldn’t have used that term because I was looking for things that are crafted more along the lines that you are talking about do you have the game posted somewhere the screenshot you shared was interesting looking

replies.author: HoboSteeveJacko
replies.body:
There is a contest for games that used AI to create games and the due date is July 31st posted on glitch. Im planning to do one last update to remove a few dev tools ive built into my game then test and post if it doesn't fail the test.  I'll try to remember to post a link when I'm done. Im grateful for any eyes and opinions that are founded on details about the game, rather then generic "ai slop" comments. Be constructive or the opinion and comments will be taken with the same face value they have directed at the screenshots or clips my game or well all games. Everyone deserves constructive feedback rather then vague complaints. 

Sorry to get a little agro. Just very used to having to defend my work. Ive never got a complaint by someone taking the time to actually try it just people willing to attack without reason.

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
I don't think anyone knows of one at the moment, The first wave just happened on next fest and theres an AI hate wave community that's been attacking a lot of the titles in it that have AI tags. 

  
The other problem thats happening aswell is we've nearly perfected ways to make 2d assets consistently and animations for them are hit or miss. 

3D projects are significantly harder if theres more complexity to them than just running around, collecting coins/keys and attacking. So theres much fewer of them. 

  
Personally, Im pushing AI hard through 3D tooling and seeing what its outputs are capable of getting through days of grueling over its outputs and fixing things and its like 70% there sometimes. Othertimes like 50%. With Sol & Fable, Im still inconclusive since im expanding more into experimental territory at the moment before id judge if we are closer to a 3D AI game dev situation where there may be a surge of good 3D products.

comments.author: Moist_Signal_5080
comments.body: The issue is public reception. When someone ends up making something they think is good, and think it might have the potential to sell, the last thing they want to do is be seen posting in Aigamedev. Even if their whole game is vibe coded. Their safest route to to have a vague AI disclosure and hope it doesn’t hurt them too much.

replies.author: Moist_Signal_5080
replies.body: Yeah it can be discouraging. Most places outside of AI  groups, like to shit on you for it.  It’s rough to be among the first wave of AI developers as far as perception goes. Once your game is targeted, there’s unfortunately no way of coming back it feels.

replies.author: dixon_sider
replies.body:
How long has vibe coding been a real possibility? Not very long. Maybe a couple years and that's an iffy maybe. 

How long would it take to make a good vibe coded game? I can't imagine it's going to be much faster than hand typing. 

How much time do you spend actually typing code? 10% of your dev time? 20%? I imagine a lot of the real dev time sinks are still going to exist.

All you need is a ln actual good game to be "vibe coded". Which all depends on how you define vibe code. If the person making the game is just prompting and not thinking or doing the difficult stuff, then it's never going to be good. If you defi e vibe code as 90 to 100% AI generated code, then we will see legit good vibe coded games.
